messages:
Maya (CS): Hey team — following up on yesterday's outage (root: 1812345678). Customer reported errors when hitting /v1/generate. I'm drafting the customer follow-up and want timeline + mitigation notes to include. Please add short bullets we can share.

IncidentBot: Incident declared: High - Token generation errors (service: inference-api). Pages fired at 2026-03-12T22:14:48Z. Oncall: Alex

Alex (Oncall): Short timeline from my side:
- 22:14 - alert firing, increased 5xx for region us-west-2
- 22:16 - I rolled the inference pool (graceful drain + restart)
- 22:22 - partial recovery, errors down ~80%
- 22:40 - full recovery after kernel patch and traffic shift
Notes: cause looked like a memory leak in the latest AVX kernel when sequences > 4k triggered a bad code path.

Riley (SRE): RCA draft bullets for customer email:
- What happened: Automated health checks and external customer requests experienced 500s due to an inference runtime kernel regression.
- Impact: A subset of requests in us-west-2 with long sequences (>= 4k tokens) observed elevated error rates and latency spikes. ~2% of total requests in the window affected.
- Mitigation: Oncall rolled the worker pool to an older kernel, and we shifted traffic to warm spare capacity while a hotfix was built.
- Timeline (short): detection 22:14, mitigation 22:22, rollback/hotfix 22:40, post-mortem 03:10 next day.

Jordan (Infra): Preventative actions to propose:
- Add a sequence-length gate in the routing layer to throttle/route >4k sequences to a safer fallback path with smaller batch sizes.
- Add runtime canary that exercises AVX kernel code paths on deploy (small synthetic workloads).
- Add metric for 'kernel_oom_rate' so we alert before 5xx spike.

Maya (CS): Draft customer-facing note (first pass):
"Hi Sam — thanks for your patience. We experienced a runtime kernel regression impacting a small percentage of long-sequence requests in us-west-2 on 2026-03-12. We detected the issue at 22:14 UTC and restored full service by 22:40 UTC. Our immediate mitigation was to roll the affected workers to a stable kernel and shift traffic to spare capacity. We're shipping a permanent fix and adding routing safeguards to prevent recurrence. We apologize for the disruption — we will credit you for the impacted usage and follow up with the full RCA in 3 business days. Let us know if you need a dedicated technical sync." 

Priya (VP CS): This looks good. Add a short bullet about credit and offer for technical sync. Keep tone concise. :thumbsup:

Sam (Customer): Thanks for the quick follow-up. Can you clarify how many requests from our org were affected and whether logs for those requests will be available? We need that for our audit.

Riley (SRE): @Sam good q. We can give counts and request IDs. I'll pull a CSV of request_ids, timestamps, and error_codes limited to your org. ETA 4 hours.

Alex (Oncall): A couple internal notes for the email: keep the technical detail light but link to our detailed RCA. Example link placeholder: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1812345678. For the timeline, prefer bullets with times in UTC.

Maya (CS): Action items assigned:
- Riley: compile request-level CSV for Sam and attach (ETA 4h)
- Jordan: implement sequence-length gating and add canary plan (ETA 5 days)
- Alex: write up the kernel hotfix summary for the RCA doc (ETA 24h)
- Maya: finalize customer email and send once Riley confirms CSV (ETA 6h)

Priya (VP CS): Also include a heads-up to account managers for affected customers so they can proactively reach out.

IncidentBot: Incident marked resolved at 22:40 UTC. Post-incident review scheduled for 2026-03-15 15:00 UTC in #eng-oncall.

Maya (CS): Thanks all. I'll post the drafted customer email below once Riley uploads the CSV and ping for approvals before sending.

Alex (Oncall): One more note — we discovered a related low-rate mem spike last week that we missed. Add to postmortem action list: backfill canary coverage across all regions.

Maya (CS): Noted. Closing thread for now, will reopen with final attachments and sent timestamp. :white_check_mark:
